articles.title: Padres closer Mason Miller added to paternity list, will miss pivotal Game 3 on Tuesday vs. Brewers
articles.summary: Miller was tied for third in MLB in saves this year with 38.
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres are one game away from elimination, down 2-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLDS. They'll be without their All-Star closer as they try to extend their season.

MLB approved a roster change for San Diego, as closer Mason Miller is going on the postseason paternity list and will not be available for Game 3 on Tuesday .

The Padres replaced Miller with reliever Wandy Peralta.

The MLB playoffs come with specific roster rules. A team must submit a roster for each series. If a player is replaced during a series due to injury, he must miss that series and , if the team advances, the following series.

But Miller was added to the postseason paternity list, and there are different rules for that. He can miss a minimum of one day and a maximum of three. When he returns, he can replace Peralta without being forced to sit out another series if San Diego makes a comeback against Milwaukee.

Miller is one of baseball's best closers. He had a career-high 38 saves this season in 66 appearances and finished with a 1.67 ERA.

The 35-year-old Peralta gives the Padres an extra lefty out of the bullpen. He made 65 appearances this season and went 3-3 with a 3.61 ERA.

San Diego heads into Tuesday's Game 3 on the brink of elimination in the best-of-five series. Games 1 and 2 both came down to the wire, with the Brew Crew winning each by one run.

Miller blew the save in Game 2 , when Jackson Chourio laced a walk-off single to center that drove in both Sal Frelick and Christian Yelich, giving Milwaukee a 4-3 victory.

If the Padres lose without Miller on Tuesday, their season is over. If San Diego wins at home Tuesday, the series will continue with Game 4 on Wednesday in San Diego, and Miller would be eligible to return.

articles.title: Dodgers-Braves: Freddie Freeman was booed and robbed of a home run in his return to Atlanta. He got revenge in his next at-bat
articles.summary: Freddie Freeman delivered countless clutch moments for the home team in 12 seasons with the Atlanta Braves. On Tuesday, he delivered one for the visitors.
articles.body:
Freddie Freeman delivered countless clutch moments in the five seasons he played at Truist Park with the Atlanta Braves.

On Tuesday, he delivered one for the visitors after being greeted with boos and being robbed of a home run in Game 3 of the National League Division Series .

With his Los Angeles Dodgers holding a 2-0 lead thanks to a Kiké Hernández home run in the fourth inning, Freeman followed with one of his own two batters later.

With the bases clear and two outs in frame, Braves starter Chris Sale threw a sinker down and inside. Freeman turned on it and sent it clear over the right-field wall.

The solo shot extended the Dodgers' lead to 3-0 and and provided redemption for Freeman after he was robbed of a home run just one inning earlier.

With a man on and no outs in the third, Freeman hit a deep shot off Sale that appeared destined to clear the short fence in left field.

But Mauricio Dubón had a bead on the ball off the bat from his position in left. He leapt in front of the Dodgers' bullpen and corralled the ball before it cleared the fence.

Replay shows that the ball was almost certainly going over the fence had Dubón not gotten there to make the play.

That home-run robbery came on the heels of Freeman being greeted with boos from the Atlanta crowd, who went on to cheer his first-inning strikeout.

But Freeman is a former MVP and three-time World Series champion for a reason. He wasn't fazed by the moment or the hostile Atlanta crowd on Tuesday.

Freeman won his MVP and his first World Series title with the Braves during his 12 seasons with the franchise. Tuesday marked his first playoff game in Atlanta since he left to sign with the Dodgers, whom he has since helped lead to two World Series championships.

There will surely be a chance for Braves fans to celebrate Freeman again after he's retired. But for now, there's no love lost with a trip to the NLCS on the line.

And there's no backing down from Freeman.

articles.title: Dodgers push Braves to the brink of MLB playoff exit
articles.summary: Enrique Hernandez and Freddie Freeman smacked home runs Tuesday to power the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers over Atlanta 3-1 and to the brink of adva...
articles.body:
Enrique Hernandez and Freddie Freeman smacked home runs Tuesday to power the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers over Atlanta 3-1 and to the brink of advancing in the Major League Baseball playoffs.

A two-run blast by Hernandez and a solo shot by former Braves star Freeman in the fourth inning combined with a stellar pitching effort from Japan's Yoshinobu Yamamoto to seal Atlanta's fate.

Yamamoto, a 28-year-old right-hander, struck out 10, matching his MLB career high, while surrendering only one run on four hits over seven innings.

"I was feeling really good. I was able to control my pitches," said Yamamoto through a translator. "That's why I got the swings and misses.

"My fastball was coming out of my hand pretty good so naturally I ended up relying on it."

The Dodgers took a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five National League divisional series, which continues in Atlanta on Wednesday.

The reigning World Series champion Dodgers are trying to win a third consecutive title, something no NL club has ever done.

In a later game, the Milwaukee Brewers seek a road victory at San Diego to complete a sweep of the Padres and reach the best-of-seven NL Championship Series (NLCS) for the second consecutive year.

The Dodgers swept Milwaukee in last year's NLCS.

Yamamoto, last year's World Series Most Valuable Player, improved to 8-1 in his MLB playoff career.

Atlanta ace Chris Sale started against Yamamoto. It was only the third game in MLB playoff history, the first since 1938, with rival starters who both had closed out a World Series-clinching contest.

Sale, a 37-year-old left-hander who threw his first shutout since 2019 in August against the Dodgers, struck out seven while allowing three runs on seven hits over five innings.

After Andy Pages singled to open the fourth, Hernandez smashed a two-run homer over the left-field wall to open the scoring.

Freeman, robbed of a homer by Mauricio Dubon's leaping catch in the third inning, followed moments later with a solo homer for a 3-0 Los Angeles lead.

That gave the Dodgers their first 10 runs of the playoffs all from homers, the longest such streak to start a post-season in MLB history.

Dubon and Lane Thomas opened the Atlanta fifth with back-to-back singles and Yamamoto walked Rowdy Tellez to load the bases.

Drake Baldwin grounded out to first to drive in Dubon from third base but Ronald Acuna grounded out to end the threat.

The Braves threatened in the ninth inning after Ozzie Albies doubled off reliever Edwin Diaz and took third on a Michael Harris ground out.

Dubon then hit a fly out and Mike Yastrzemski grounded out to end the game.

Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani, a four-time MVP who has battled right biceps and left knee injuries, was dropped to fifth in the batting order, his lowest spot in six years.

The Japanese star went 0-for-2 with a walk and a strikeout.
